source_documents.title: Synthesis of Indolocarbazole‐Diketopyrrolopyrrole Dyads and Investigation of Their Photoinduced Electron Transfer Properties

conditions_studied: solution: cyclohexane, toluene, CHCl3, THF, DCM, acetonitrile (fs/ns transient absorption)

reference_evidence_units.quote: the fluorescence response of dyad 1 was quenched with a quenching efficiency of 99.9% with respect to its reference acceptor DPP 2a
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: DPP fluorescence is almost fully quenched in the dyad.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Fluorescence was also observed to be almost completely quenched in polar solvents (e.g. dichloromethane, tetrahydrofuran, acetonitrile) as compared to nonpolar solvent such as cyclohexane and toluene, which suggested that the charge transfer or electron transfer might potentially be an important deactivation channel in the dyads.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyads 1-3

reference_evidence_units.quote: Thus, initial transient spectral dynamics can be assigned to photoinduced electron transfer from ICZ donor to phenyl-DPP (2a) acceptor resulting in charge separated (CS) state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: DPP radical-anion absorption: ICZ→DPP electron transfer to a CS state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, unlike dyad 1, new ESA signature of the DPP anion radical is absent in dyad 2, suggesting partial charge transfer (CT) from donor ICZ to thiophene-DPP (3) acceptor.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad 2
reference_evidence_units.statement: No DPP anion band: partial CT rather than full charge separation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In essence, TA spectroscopy revealed that all three dyads undergo ultrafast charge separation dynamics acting as a dominant pathway for non-radiative relaxation in dichloromethane.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyads 1-3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Ultrafast charge separation is the main nonradiative channel in DCM.

reference_evidence_units.quote: On the other hand, in nonpolar toluene, instead of charge separation, we only observed a spectroscopic signature of the charge transfer
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyads
reference_evidence_units.statement: In toluene a CT state forms instead of a CS state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This indicates that the excited states of dyads are getting de-excited non-radiatively probably through electron transfer mechanism not through energy transfer pathway.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyads
reference_evidence_units.statement: Energy transfer is ruled out in favour of electron transfer.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: fs-TA shows no DPP radical anion: partial charge transfer from ICZ to the thiophene-DPP.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Polarity-dependent quenching and the paper's summary that all dyads undergo ultrafast charge separation in DCM.

contrast_group.varied_factor: aryl unit of the DPP acceptor (phenyl vs thiophene)
contrast_group.paper_difference: With phenyl-DPP the excited dyad forms a full charge-separated state (DPP radical anion); with thiophene-DPP only partial charge transfer is seen.

basis: thiophene analogue of dyad 1 from dibromo thiophene-DPP 5 (Scheme 3; DPP 5 and the ICZ unit recognised from the drawings)
structure_verification.note: The whole dyad was not recognised in one drawing; assembled from the recognised N,N'-dialkyl thiophene-DPP and ICZ units and checked against the MALDI formula.
